description: Executor.governance_state() — configured vs. actually wired (PROTOCOL_SPEC 6.6.5). `acl != null` means an ACL object is attached, NOT that ACL evaluation runs: the gates are pipeline steps, and the `internal` / `testing` / `minimal` presets remove them. Every field, the derived flag included, MUST be identical across the three SDKs for every case. The accessor is a pure read — a case that changes executor state has been driven wrong.

driver_contract.path: MUST call the real accessor on a real Executor whose strategy, ACL, handler and policy were set through the public API. Reconstructing the eight booleans in the driver asserts the driver's arithmetic, not the SDK's.
driver_contract.derived_flag_is_asserted_not_recomputed: `expected.unprotected_control_surface` MUST be compared against what the SDK returned. A driver that recomputes it from the other seven fields is green against an implementation that never computes it at all.
driver_contract.the_lookalike_case_is_the_point: `custom_step_named_acl_check_is_not_the_builtin` requires registering a strategy containing a step whose NAME is `acl_check` and whose TYPE is not the built-in gate. A driver that skips it because building one is awkward has removed the only case that distinguishes a type test from a name test.
driver_contract.purity: After each case the driver MUST call governance_state() twice and assert both returns are equal, and MUST assert no warning was emitted and no exception raised. 6.6.5.3 forbids the accessor from enforcing, warning, throwing or mutating.
driver_contract.liveness: For at least one case the driver MUST call the accessor, mutate the executor (attach an ACL or swap the strategy), and call again — the second result MUST reflect the change. A cached value passes every static case.

test_cases.note: sys_modules.enabled=false — nothing registered, nothing to gate.
The 6 read modules with no ACL. An information-disclosure question, not a control-plane one — unprotected_control_surface MUST be false because there is no write surface at all.
All 9 registered, nothing attached. The condition the flag exists to report.
ACL attached to an executor running `standard`, which contains acl_check.

The case that motivates the whole accessor: set_acl() on an executor running `internal`, which removes acl_check. acl_configured is true, builtin_acl_gate_wired is false, and the surface is unprotected. `acl != null` reports this as protected.
ExecutionPolicy(strict=true) with no handler on `standard`: the approval gate fails closed, so the surface is gated even though approval_handler_configured is false.
Same policy, `internal` strategy. policy_strict is true and the gate is still not wired, so it enforces nothing.

A custom step named `acl_check` that never consults an ACL, in a strategy otherwise like standard. builtin_acl_gate_wired MUST be false. This is the case that decides whether an implementation detects gates by type or by name — and a name-based implementation fails it in the ONE direction the flag must never fail in: reporting a gate that is not there.
The fully-gated control case. Without it, an implementation hardcoding unprotected_control_surface=true passes most of the cases above.
